title: Budget and Revenue
text:
Do bigger budget films earn more money? Figure 1 plots the production budget of a film against its revenue

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget(USD)")
plt.show







Figure 1: Production budget against revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
Do longer films get better ratings? Figure 1 plots runtime against ratings

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("Rating (0 to 10)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime (minutes) against rating

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]


bond_sorted = bond.sort_values("year")
plt.plot(bond_sorted["year"], bond_sorted["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (USD in millions)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of the Bond films over time (USD)
